additional_concerns: Footnote 4 is supplied in db43e253bea18.u30.8235; the advertising claim's uncertainty incorrectly calls it missing. The Advertising Guidelines and their supplementary FAQs and guidance are missing.

The Code of Conduct paragraph 3.11 and the answer to question 1 of the SFC's 30 September 2010 FAQs, identified by footnotes 2 and 3, are not supplied as external dependencies. Their detailed classifications remain unchecked.

node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e puts offering in scope; nodes node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5, node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5, node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 put promotional conditions in scope. Consequently, absent offering or promotion can yield OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than the typed question's negative prohibition answer or positive selected-control compliance answer. Whether that narrower assessment domain is intended remains unresolved.

The offer-level candidates combine an offer-wide promotional link with an existential non-discount gift classification. They should require that the same gift component has the relevant promotional link; otherwise a mixed offer could produce an unsupported prohibition.

The circular defines distributors by reference to SFC-authorised funds, supporting that contextual scope. Paragraph 3.11's quoted investment-product language is broader; these candidates should not be presented as exhaustive implementations of the Code outside the circular's scope.

A gift-control result does not establish compliance with section 103 or advertising requirements. Conversely, section 103 authorisation or exemption supplies no stated permission to offer a prohibited gift.
No operative date interval is supplied in the retained text. The candidates' temporal-basis statements do not establish effective dates or resolve competing temporal interpretations.
